criteria.evidence: The file service is configured (via the Hub service command/args) with a single allowed test directory; the file MCP only resolves paths under that directory, so the scope is fixed unless the user edits the args explicitly.
criteria.source: isolated mcp.json fs service args (t009-allowed); fixture file_allowed; servers/file-mcp.mjs
criteria.limitations: Expanding the scope requires the user to change the service command/args; no separate UI control beyond the existing service editor.

criteria.evidence: Reading the in-scope file returned its exact content ('allowed-content-ok'), i.e. a safe tool operation inside the allowed directory succeeds.
criteria.source: tests/acceptance/check.py check_009 file_allowed; manual gateway probe
criteria.limitations: Demonstrated for a read of a known safe file; it is not an exhaustive sweep of every in-scope operation.

criteria.evidence: Reading the outside sentinel returned isError:true with 'Access denied: <path> is outside the allowed directory', so the out-of-scope read was refused by the executing end; the sentinel checksum was unchanged after the attempt.
criteria.source: tests/acceptance/check.py check_009 file_denied + sentinel hash; servers/file-mcp.mjs
criteria.limitations: Covers an out-of-scope read; traversal/symlink bypass variants are addressed below rather than exhaustively.

criteria.evidence: The scope check resolves the target path with node path.resolve before comparing against the allowed directory, so '..' traversal normalises and is rejected; the decision is enforced by the file process, not by prompts or on-screen wording.
criteria.limitations: Symlink-based escapes are not separately proven; the enforcement is path-normalisation based and the supplementary VT-09 cases remain the place for exhaustive traversal/link evidence.

changes.summary: Added an isolated test file MCP (stdio) that reads text only inside a single allowed directory and returns an explicit 'Access denied' rejection for any path outside it, using path.resolve to neutralise '..' traversal. Added T-009 fixture fields: outside_sentinel (the out-of-scope file), file_allowed (in-scope read with expected content) and file_denied (out-of-scope read expecting a denial containing 'denied').
